html:
SMTO-SKL-0085 — SMTO doesn't recognize that time zone

GUID: ad7ddb97-a70f-5ab3-9235-b12bd7061b12
Slug: microsoft365-invalid-timezone
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The time zone given for this calendar request isn't one SMTO or Microsoft understands, so SMTO couldn't work out the times. Nothing was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell SMTO the time zone as a region and city, for example “America/New_York”, “Europe/London” or “Asia/Kolkata”. This form is understood everywhere, while short names like “EST” or local nicknames can be unclear.
  2. If you prefer Windows names, use one of the common ones such as “Eastern Standard Time” or “GMT Standard Time”. SMTO only knows a short list of Windows time zone names.
  3. Ask SMTO to repeat the calendar request with that time zone. Nothing was created the first time, so repeating it won't make a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows or creates the event at the right local time.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time zone you used, to the person who manages SMTO; the computer running SMTO may need its time zone data updated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 calendar zone resolution failed: the timezone is neither an installed IANA identifier nor one of the supported Windows aliases in calendar.WINDOWS, or Microsoft Graph returned ErrorInvalidTimeZone/InvalidTimeZone.

What this means

  • Local timezone resolution fails or Graph returns ErrorInvalidTimeZone/InvalidTimeZone. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Local timezone resolution fails or Graph returns ErrorInvalidTimeZone/InvalidTimeZone.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested IANA/Windows alias with the installed mapping and recorded provider response.

How to fix it

  • Pass an installed IANA timezone identifier such as America/New_York or Europe/London, or one of the Windows aliases in src/agent_runtime/skills/microsoft365/calendar.py (WINDOWS); for other Windows names use the equivalent IANA identifier. If the name resolved locally but Graph returned ErrorInvalidTimeZone, use a common IANA identifier or a listed Windows alias; if a valid IANA name fails locally, install or update the Server's tzdata.
  • Supply an installed IANA timezone or one of the documented Windows timezone aliases.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported timezone resolves consistently at both boundaries.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.
